terra.problem: The seating-chart joke presents a family reunion as forthcoming, though the passage says nothing about one.
“They're sisters” follows a sentence about Amasa and Joab, making it sound as though the two men are sisters rather than their mothers.
Being cousins does not establish that Amasa and Joab know each other. Even cousins can be strangers.
“Nobody's asked” goes beyond the text, which does not say whether anyone asked for supplies.
David says he will march out, but “the king is headed to the field” presents that intention as an action. He does not march out.
The joke puts down bosses as a group by saying it is rare for one to take advice from a team.
“Close in sound” is not an accurate observation about “fairly” and “gently.”
“When you're in a forest, always look up” is a generic aside rather than a clear or useful joke.
“That's why” makes the man's expectation that Joab would abandon him the sole reason he would not strike Absalom. He also cites the king's command.
“I think he's seen how these things go” invents an unrecorded experience for the man.
Stopping their pursuit does not establish that the troops do not go deeper into the forest at all.
The passage says the Israelites flee to their homes, not that nobody is marching together anymore.
“Nobody's planning a coronation” asserts something the passage does not say.
David stood by the gate when the troops marched out, but the passage does not say he is still there when the Israelites flee.
